title: The Trung Sisters Rise Up

parts.text: Hello, my little friends! Do you know who the first two women were who led an army to chase away invaders and win back the land for the Viet people?
Today, Huy Tells Tales will tell you the story of how the Trung Sisters rose up.
Once upon a time, almost two thousand years ago, our country was ruled by the Han people from the faraway north.
The Han officials made our people hand over lots and lots of rice and silk. The Viet people had a very hard life.

In Me Linh district, between Ba Vi Mountain and Tam Dao Mountain, there lived two sisters named Trung Trac and Trung Nhi. Their father was a Lac lord, a descendant of the Hung kings, but he had passed away young.
Sister, our silkworms have spun golden silk all over the whole tray!
You are so clever with your hands. Tomorrow we will weave silk as a gift for Mother.
The sisters' mother was Lady Man Thien. She raised her children all by herself. She taught her two daughters to grow mulberry trees and raise silkworms, and she taught them martial arts too.
My dear children, learn to weave silk so you can take care of yourselves, and learn to hold a spear so you can protect your village.
Yes, Mother! We will always remember your words!
Every morning on the riverside field, the two sisters practiced martial arts hard. The sound of their wooden spears clacking together rang out, clack, clack.
Sister, can you block this spear move of mine?
You are very quick, but I am even quicker than you!
At that time, the Han court sent an official named To Dinh to be the governor of Giao Chi. He was greedy and cruel.
Every home must hand over more rice and more silk to me!
Sir, this year the harvest failed. The people have nothing left to give.
If you don't pay, I will send you all away to do forced labor!
That was not all. The Han soldiers also made the Viet people give up their wedding customs and the clothes of their grandparents, and follow the Han ways instead.
From now on, everyone must follow the rules of the Han people!
These customs were handed down by our ancestors for ages. Oh heavens, how can they make us give them up?
Trung Trac and Trung Nhi traveled through the villages. Seeing the people suffer, they felt great sorrow. The two sisters were strong by nature, and they would not bow to To Dinh's harsh laws.
To Dinh has bullied our people far too much!
Sister, we cannot sit still any longer!
When she grew up, Trung Trac married Thi Sach, the son of a Lac lord in Chu Dien district, right across the Day River. Thi Sach was a brave and mighty man.
My dear wife, our two families share the same goal, and we both care for the good people.
I promise to protect our homeland together with you.
The two families quietly joined hands with Lac lords everywhere. Lady Man Thien also went to meet the chiefs around the region.
We are the children and grandchildren of the Hung kings. How can we bow our heads forever?
Many chiefs nodded and promised to rise up together.
The news reached To Dinh. He feared the Viet people would rise up, so he did something cruel.
Thi Sach dares to stand against me. Seize him at once!
And so, Thi Sach was killed by To Dinh.
Hearing the terrible news, Trung Trac was heartbroken.
My husband, oh my husband!
But then she wiped away her tears and looked out at the river.
I will surely avenge my family and win back my country!
The two sisters led their troops to the mouth of the Hat River to get ready. Villagers eagerly came to forge spears, carve arrows, and make crossbows.
I am old but still strong. Let me forge spears for the Two Ladies to fight the invaders!
Thank you, Grandfather! When the whole village works together, any enemy will be afraid.
Something special happened. Many women came to join the Two Ladies, such as Le Chan, Thanh Thien, and Bat Nan. Every one of them was skilled in martial arts and brave.
We women also know how to hold a spear and defend our country!
With you, my sisters, my heart is as steady as Ba Vi Mountain.
On the fourth day of the ninth month, on the rocky shore at the mouth of the Hat River, the Two Ladies gathered the generals for a solemn oath. Flags fluttered and everyone stood straight and proud.
First, I vow to wash away the shame of our enemies!
Second, I vow to rebuild the old kingdom of the Hung kings!
Third, I cry out for justice for my husband. Fourth, I vow to finish this great task completely!
Their vow echoed across the whole river.
We vow to drive out the Han invaders!
We vow to win back our homeland!

In the spring of the year forty, the day to march out had come. Trung Trac was still in mourning for her husband, but she wore a beautiful gown and combed her hair neatly, and she stood shining before the army.
Sister, you are still in mourning for your husband. Why are you dressed so beautifully today?
Fighting the invaders cannot wait. If I looked gloomy, the soldiers would lose their spirit. I dress beautifully so our army shines even brighter, and the enemy will tremble when they see us!
The generals all listened and admired her.
You truly deserve to lead us, Sister!
Boom, boom, boom! The bronze drums rang out. The army of the Two Ladies marched forward with a rumble, their spears gleaming in the sunshine.
Brothers and sisters, forward!
Drive out To Dinh!
In the first battle, the rebels attacked the enemy fort at Me Linh. The Han soldiers did not even have time to pick up their spears before they were in a panic.
The Two Ladies' army is here! Run away quickly!
The enemy fell over and scattered in all directions. The Me Linh fort was won by the rebels.
After the victory, the Two Ladies marched on Co Loa Citadel. The people there opened the gates and came out with food and water to welcome them.
The Two Ladies are here, everyone!
Do not be afraid, good people. We have come to drive the invaders away for you!
From Co Loa, the rebels rowed their boats across the river and attacked Luy Lau, where To Dinh had his headquarters.
Sister, Luy Lau Citadel is right in front of us!
Forward! We will not let To Dinh escape!
Inside the headquarters, To Dinh shook with fear. The Two Ladies' army struck as fast as the wind, and he had no time to fight back.
How did their army get here so fast?
Sir, the city gate is about to break!
Afraid of being recognized, To Dinh quickly shaved his head, shaved off his beard, and even threw away his official seal.
Shave off all my beard and hair! Throw this seal away too. Let's run!
The once bossy official hid among the soldiers and ran away with his head down. He looked so funny.
To Dinh ran all the way back to Nam Hai, in the land of the Han. Later, even the Han emperor scolded him for being greedy and cowardly, and he was thrown into prison.
News of the victory flew far and wide. The people of Cuu Chan, Nhat Nam, and Hop Pho all rose up to join in. Before long, the Two Ladies had won back sixty-five citadels.
The invaders have all run away! Our homeland belongs to us Viet people again!
The Lac lords together honored Trung Trac as queen. She set up her capital at Me Linh, and Trung Nhi became Vice Queen to help her sister.
We ask that Sister Trung Trac be crowned queen!
Long live Queen Trung!
Queen Trung stood before all the people, her voice warm yet carrying far.
From now on, our people may live by the customs of our grandparents. I give thanks to our ancestors, the Hung kings.
I promise to stay with you, Sister, and keep our land safe!
For more than three years, the Viet people ruled their homeland themselves. After that, the Han court sent a general named Ma Vien with a huge army to attack.
Even if the enemy is many, we sisters will never bow our heads!
I will always be by your side!
The Two Ladies fought to the very end at Cam Khe, then rose up to heaven beside the Hat River, leaving a shining example that lasts for all time.

Today, beside the Hat River, there is still the Hat Mon Temple to honor the Two Ladies. Nearby is Ha Loi village, their mother's hometown, and Men Shrine, which honors Lady Man Thien, the mother of the Two Ladies.

The history books call Trung Trac the Trung Queen, and the people lovingly call the Two Ladies the Two Saints of Me Linh. People still come to light incense and remember the great deeds of these two heroes.
My dear little friends, the Trung Sisters show us that girls are brave and talented too, just as much as anyone. Let us love our homeland, care for everyone, and stay united together, all right?
If you liked this story, please remember to subscribe to the channel Huy Kể Chuyện to hear many more fun stories from Vietnamese history. See you again soon!

facts.claim: Trưng Trắc là con gái Lạc tướng huyện Mê Linh, lấy chồng là Thi Sách, con Lạc tướng huyện Chu Diên
Mẹ Hai Bà là bà Man Thiện, góa chồng sớm, dạy hai con trồng dâu nuôi tằm và võ nghệ, giúp liên kết các quan lang ủng hộ khởi nghĩa
Thái thú Tô Định sang Giao Chỉ năm 34, tàn bạo tham lam, tăng thuế khóa phục dịch; nhà Hán ép người Việt đổi phong tục cưới hỏi, y phục
Theo Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, Tô Định giết Thi Sách, khiến Trưng Trắc càng gấp rút khởi binh
Hội thề ở bãi đá cửa sông Hát ngày mồng 4 tháng 9 năm 39 với bốn lời thề ghi trong Thiên Nam ngữ lục
Nhiều tướng lĩnh của cuộc khởi nghĩa là phụ nữ như Lê Chân, Thánh Thiên, Bát Nàn
Khi xuất quân, Trưng Trắc còn tang chồng nhưng mặc đẹp để tăng nhuệ khí quân sĩ
Nghĩa quân đánh Mê Linh, chiếm Cổ Loa rồi hạ trị sở Luy Lâu; Tô Định cạo tóc râu, vứt ấn tín, trốn về Nam Hải và sau bị vua Hán trị tội
Cửu Chân, Nhật Nam, Hợp Phố hưởng ứng, Hai Bà lấy được 65 thành; Trưng Trắc lên ngôi vua, đóng đô ở Mê Linh, Trưng Nhị làm Phó Vương
Hơn ba năm sau, Mã Viện sang đánh, Hai Bà chiến đấu và mất ở Cấm Khê, truyền thuyết kể Hai Bà gieo mình xuống sông Hát
Dấu tích còn lại gồm đền Hát Môn, làng Hạ Lôi, Cấm Khê và Miếu Mèn thờ bà Man Thiện; thần tích gọi Hai Bà là Mê Linh Nhị Thánh

look: Thời Bắc thuộc lần 1, khoảng năm 34–43, văn hóa Lạc Việt hậu Đông Sơn. Trưng Trắc: áo cánh ngắn xẻ ngực khép kín màu nâu đỏ, bên trong mặc yếm, váy quấn dài tới mắt cá màu chàm, thắt lưng vải có tua buông trước bụng; tóc búi cao quấn khăn, đeo khuyên tai và vòng tay bằng đồng hoặc đá; khi ra trận khoác giáp da thuộc, đeo kiếm đồng ngắn, cầm giáo đồng; ngày xuất quân mặc áo màu tươi, có dải lụa thắt lưng rực rỡ. Trưng Nhị: trang phục giống chị, tông xanh lá và nâu, trẻ trung hơn, cầm giáo hoặc nỏ. Bà Man Thiện: áo cánh nâu sẫm, váy đen dài, khăn vấn đầu, tóc điểm bạc, đứng bên nong tằm, khung cửi. Thi Sách: áo cánh nâu, quần hoặc khố vải dài kín có thắt lưng, tóc búi tó hoặc cắt ngắn, đeo rìu đồng ở hông. Lê Chân và các nữ tướng: áo cánh, váy quấn, giáp da, khăn quấn đầu, cầm giáo, nỏ. Nghĩa quân và dân làng: áo cánh nâu, khố vải dài kín đáo, tóc ngắn hoặc búi tó, chân đất; cầm giáo đồng, nỏ, rìu, khiên mây; có người đội mũ cắm lông chim như hình trên trống đồng. Ông lão, bà cụ: áo nâu bạc màu, khăn vấn. Tô Định: quan nhà Hán, áo giao lĩnh vạt chéo rộng tay màu đỏ sẫm, thắt đai, đội mũ quan đen, râu dài, đeo ấn tín bằng đồng có dây; sau khi chạy trốn đầu cạo trọc, mặt nhẵn, mặc áo lính lấm lem. Lính Hán: áo giáp vảy sẫm màu, mũ trụ, cầm kích và khiên, cờ đen viền đỏ. Nhà cửa: nhà sàn gỗ mái tranh cong vút hình thuyền kiểu trên trống đồng Đông Sơn, cầu thang gỗ, gầm sàn có nong tằm, cối giã gạo; ruộng lúa nước, đồi dâu, sông Hát và sông Đáy, núi Ba Vì xa xa. Dinh Luy Lâu và thành Cổ Loa: tường lũy đất cao, cổng gỗ, chòi canh, dinh quan Hán mái cong lợp tranh hoặc ngói đất nung thô. Đồ vật: trống đồng, thạp đồng, giáo, rìu, mũi tên đồng, nỏ, thuyền độc mộc, lò rèn, nong nia, khung cửi dệt lụa, kén tằm vàng. Bãi thề Hát Môn: bãi đá ven sông, cờ vải nhiều màu, trống đồng. Tránh: áo dài, áo tứ thân, nón quai thao, nón lá, gạch nung và tường gạch, chùa chiền, đồ sứ men, giấy và chữ viết trên biển hiệu, kính, vải in hoa, voi chiến, áo hở hang; cảnh đánh nhau không máu, giặc chỉ ngã rạp hay bỏ chạy.
